texts.preamble: Shaik Tameem Ahmed vs The State Of Telangana on 13 October, 2020 Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy Bench: Raghvendra Singh Chauhan, B.Vijaysen Reddy High Court For The State Of Telangana The Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Raghvendra Singh Chauhan And The Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy Writ Petition No.13245 of 2020 Date: 13.10.2020 Between Shaik Tameem Ahmed. ... Petitioner And The State of Telangana, Rep. by its Principal Secretary to Government, General Administration ((Spl. (Law & Order), Secretariat, Hyderabad and others. ...Respondents Counsel for the petitioner : Mr. P. Trivikram Reddy Counsel for the respondents : Mr. T. Srikanth Reddy Gp for Home The Court made the following: 2 Order:
texts.facts: Detenu moved bail of 2018 VI Town PS petition before II IPC in Cr.No.621 AJMFC, Nizamabad of 2018. His and he was granted arrest was bail and released on regularized 19.03.2019. through PT warrant. 3. Cr.No.223 Shahinayathgunj u/s 379 03.12.2019 Detenu moved bail PS petition before XVI of 2018 IPC in Cr.No.621 ACMM, Hyderabad and of 2018. His he was granted bail arrest was and released on regularized 06.05.2019. through PT warrant. 4. Cr.No.621 Panjagutta PS u/s 379 03.12.2018 Detenu moved bail petition vide of 2019 IPC CRLMP.No.4254 of 2018. Despite opposition by APP, the detenu was granted bail and released on 06.05.2019. 6. All the four criminal cases registered under Section379 IPC relate to theft of motor cycles. The offences are committed against specific individuals and in the limits of different police stations. The first, third and fourth crimes relate to three different police stations in Hyderabad. The second crime relates to police station in Nizamabad District. 7. The impugned detention order is passed on the premise that the inhabitants of the locality wherein crimes have been registered got panicked and scared fearing thefts. Thus, the activities of the detenu adversely affected public order leaving large sections of people under the grip of fear and scare. Further, the detenu moved bail applications in all the four cases and conditional bails have been granted. Hence, it is alleged that there is possibility of the detenu committing similar offences. 8. As stated supra, the offences are committed against specific individuals. The aggrieved parties/victims are individuals and not members of particular community or public at large. Shaik Tameem Ahmed vs The State Of Telangana on 13 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8854707/ 3
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that there is no proximity and nexus between the cases relied upon by the detaining authority. There is no material to substantiate and justify for treating the detenu as 'Goonda' within the meaning of Section 2(g) of the Act. Further, the alleged activities of the detenu come within the purview of maintenance of law and order and not public order. Hence, the impugned detention order is unsustainable and liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 4. Per contra, the learned Government Pleader for Home submitted that the detenu answers the description of 'Goonda' as defined in Section 2(g) of the Act. The distinction between "law and order" and "public order" is succinctly laid in PUSHKAR MUKHERJEE v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL1, the Supreme Court held as under: The question to be considered in the present case is whether grounds (a), (b) and (e) served on Subhas Chandra Bose are grounds which are relevant to "the maintenance of public order". All these grounds relate to cases of assault on solitary individuals either by knife or by using crackers and it is difficult (1969) 1 SCC 10 to accept the contention of the respondent that these grounds have any relevance or proximate connection with the maintenance of public order. In ARUN GHOSH v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL2 the Supreme Court held as under: It means therefore that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of law and order or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the public order is a question of degree and the extent of the reach of the act upon the society. Shaik Tameem Ahmed vs The State Of Telangana on 13 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8854707/ 4 The French distinguish law and order and public order by designating the latter as order publique. The latter expression has been recognized as meaning something more than ordinary maintenance of law and order. In a recent decision of this Court in RAPOLU MAHALAKSHMI v. STATE OF TELANGANA3 it was held as under: 12. Every violation of criminal law does cause a rippled in the society. But the ripples can be calmed down by use of normal Criminal Justice System. It is only when an offence strikes the society, like a tsunami, that as a weapon of the last resort, the detaining authority is justified in invoking the powers under preventive detention laws. 13. Therefore, while invoking the magical formula of preventive detention, the detaining authority is required to firstly consider whether the offences, allegedly committed by the detenu, can be dealt with within the normal course of Criminal Justice System or not? The detaining authority should also examine whether the release of the detenu can be prevented by opposing his bail applications or not? Whether his detention under judicial custody can be ensured or not? Shaik Tameem Ahmed vs The State Of Telangana on 13 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8854707/ 5 14.
